name: Abigail

seo.title: Abigail in the Bible: the wife who stopped David, and her story
seo.description: Abigail in plain words: Nabal's wise wife, the gifts and the plea that kept David from bloodshed, her marriage to David, and the myths.

band.lede: She rode out with bread and wine to meet David and his 400 swords. Her words kept him from bloodshed, and he blessed her for it.

picture.alt: A painting by Antonio Molinari: Abigail, a young woman with fair hair and a pearl earring, in a white blouse and a yellow shawl, looks up pleading at David. He stands before her in a silver helmet and green armour under a red cloak, with soldiers behind him. Beside her are a donkey, a servant, a basket of loaves and a camel's head against a blue sky.
picture.credit: David and Abigail, Antonio Molinari, Venice, late 1600s. Public domain.

who: Abigail was the wife of Nabal, a rich and harsh sheep farmer at Carmel, in Judah. When Nabal insulted David, David set out with 400 armed men to kill every male in his house. Abigail rode out to meet him with gifts, fell at his feet and talked him out of it. After Nabal died, she married David.

tidbits.text: An “abigail” was once English for a lady's maid. Merriam-Webster traces the word to a maid in a play of 1616. The 1911 *Britannica* traces it to her: she called herself David's “handmaid”.
The rabbis counted her one of the four most beautiful women who ever lived, with Sarah, Rahab and Esther.
In the 1560s Maarten van Heemskerck designed prints of the eight Beatitudes. For “Blessed are the peacemakers” he chose Abigail at David's feet.

facts.label: In the Bible
facts.text: One chapter, **1 Samuel 25**. After it she is named only in lists: as David's wife in 1 Samuel 27 and 30 and 2 Samuel 2, and as a mother in 2 Samuel 3 and 1 Chronicles 3.

facts.label: Home
facts.text: **Carmel**, a town in the hill country of Judah, near Maon. It is not the Mount Carmel of Elijah.

facts.label: Husbands
facts.text: **Nabal**, a rich sheep farmer, harsh to everyone. Then **David**, still an outlaw hiding from King Saul when he married her.

facts.label: Son
facts.text: **Chileab**, David's second son, born at Hebron. Chronicles calls him **Daniel**.

facts.label: Also called
facts.text: **Abigail of Carmel**, and **the widow of Nabal**. A **prophetess**, in the Talmud.

facts.label: Died
facts.text: The Bible does not say when or where. It leaves her at Hebron, the mother of David's second son.

facts.label: In art
facts.text: Painters show her before David, with her loaves and wine loaded on donkeys, as at the top of this page. Most have her kneeling.

portrait.alt: A detail of an oil sketch by Rubens: Abigail kneels on the ground in a grey-blue gown and a thin veil, one hand on her breast and the other held out. David, in armour and a red cloak, bends forward and takes her hand. Two of her maidens stand behind her, and soldiers in helmets behind him, under a golden sky.

said.lede: David, the historian Josephus, three of the Fathers and the rabbis, in their own words.

quotes.q: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, Who sent you to meet me this day! Blessed is your discernment, and blessed are you, because today you kept me from bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand.

She replied to those that came, that she was not worthy to touch his feet; however, she came, with all her servants, and became his wife, having received that honor on account of her wise and righteous course of life.
quotes.who: Josephus, the Jewish historian, in the 90s AD

cite.text: Josephus, *Antiquities of the Jews*, book 6, chapter 13

quotes.q: So much was David pleased that he blessed her who intervened, because he was restrained from his desire for revenge.
quotes.who: Ambrose of Milan, teaching his clergy to hold back anger

cite.text: Ambrose, *On the Duties of the Clergy*, Book 1, chapter 21

quotes.q: He gave up his threats, lightened the sentence, and preferred to be regarded as a breaker of his word rather than to keep his pledged oath by cruelly executing it

moments.title: “Who is David?”
moments.text: Nabal of Maon was very rich, with three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. His wife was Abigail. “She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.” David, hiding from King Saul in the wilderness, sent ten young men to Nabal at shearing time. His men had guarded Nabal's shepherds, and he asked for whatever Nabal could spare. Nabal answered, “Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse?” So David told his men, “Strap on your swords!” About four hundred went with him.

moments.title: “Consider carefully what you must do”
moments.text: One of Nabal's young men went to Abigail, not to his master. David's men had been very good to them, he told her. “They were a wall around us, both day and night.” But Nabal had screamed at David's messengers. “Now consider carefully what you must do,” he said, “because disaster looms over our master and all his household. For he is such a scoundrel that nobody can speak to him!”

moments.title: She hurried
moments.text: “Then Abigail hurried.” She took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five butchered sheep, five measures of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs, and loaded them on donkeys. She sent her young men on first: “Go ahead of me. I will be right behind you.” “But she did not tell her husband Nabal.” Meanwhile David was swearing that by morning not one male of Nabal's house would be left alive.

moments.title: At David's feet
moments.text: Riding down into a ravine, she met David and his men coming toward her. She got off the donkey, fell facedown and bowed. Then she took the blame on herself and pleaded. The LORD had held David back from bloodshed, she said. One day He would make him ruler over Israel, and then he would have no needless killing on his conscience. Her words are below. David blessed her, and took her gift. “Go home in peace,” he said. “See, I have heeded your voice and granted your request.”

moments.when: That night, and the morning after
moments.title: “Like a stone”
moments.text: When she came home, Nabal was holding “a feast fit for a king,” in high spirits and very drunk. “So she told him nothing until morning light.” In the morning, sober, he heard it all from her. “His heart failed within him, and he became like a stone.” About ten days later, “the LORD struck Nabal dead.”

moments.title: David's wife
moments.text: When David heard, he blessed the LORD, Who had “restrained His servant from evil.” Then he sent word to Abigail at Carmel, asking her to become his wife. She bowed facedown and called herself his servant, ready to wash his servants' feet. Then she hurried onto a donkey and, with five of her maidens, followed his messengers. David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel.

moments.title: Taken captive
moments.text: With Saul still hunting him, David took his men and their families to Achish, the Philistine king of Gath, who gave him the town of Ziklag. Abigail and Ahinoam went with him. While the men were away, Amalekites raided Ziklag, burned it and carried off the women and children. David's men wept “until they had no strength left to weep,” and spoke of stoning him. “But David found strength in the LORD his God.” He pursued the raiders and recovered everything, “including his two wives.”

moments.title: The mother of Chileab
moments.text: After Saul died, David went up to Hebron with his two wives, and the men of Judah anointed him king. There Abigail bore his second son, Chileab. Here the Bible's story of her ends.

words.note: Abigail wrote nothing. These are her words as 1 Samuel records them. Outside the quiz's own section, every Bible line on this page is from the Berean Standard Bible.

feature.q: Should someone pursue you and seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound securely by the LORD your God in the bundle of the living.
feature.ctx: Jewish gravestones most often end with five Hebrew letters that echo this line: “May his soul be bound in the bundle of life.”

quotes.q: My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.
quotes.who: Her first words, at David's feet.

quotes.q: My lord should pay no attention to this scoundrel Nabal, for he lives up to his name: His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him.
Please forgive your servant's offense, for the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD's battles. May no evil be found in you as long as you live.
quotes.who: To the future king, still an outlaw.

quotes.q: When the LORD has done for my lord all the good He promised, and when He has appointed you ruler over Israel, then my lord will have no remorse or guilt of conscience over needless bloodshed and revenge. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your servant.
Here is your servant, ready to serve and to wash the feet of my lord's servants.
quotes.who: Her answer when David asked her to marry him.

myths.truth: Two women in the Bible are called Abigail. This one was Nabal's wife, then David's. The other was David's sister, the mother of Amasa, whom Absalom made commander of his army. Chronicles lists her with her sister: “Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail.”

myths.claim: She kept what she had done from her husband.
myths.truth: She set out without a word to him. But she did not keep it from him. That night he was very drunk, so she waited, and in the morning she told him everything. Gregory the Great praised her twice for it: she “laudably kept silence about his fault” while he was drunk, and “as laudably told him of it” once he was sober.

cite.text: 1 Samuel 25:19, 36-37; Gregory the Great, *Pastoral Rule*, Part III, chapter 16

circle.name: David
circle.text: The outlaw she met in the ravine. He blessed her for stopping him, married her after Nabal's death, and was made king at Hebron with her beside him.

circle.name: Nabal
circle.text: Her first husband, a rich sheep farmer of Maon. His name means Fool, she told David, and he lived up to it. He died about ten days after she told him what she had done.

circle.name: Nabal's young man
circle.text: One of the shepherds. When his master screamed at David's men, he went to Abigail instead, because “nobody can speak to him.”

circle.name: Ahinoam of Jezreel
circle.text: David's other wife. The two were carried off together from Ziklag and rescued together. Her son Amnon was David's firstborn.

circle.name: Chileab
circle.text: Her son, David's second, born at Hebron. Chronicles calls him Daniel. The Bible tells nothing more of him.

saint.big: No church keeps a feast day for her. She has no day in the Catholic or Orthodox calendars of saints, and none in the Anglican or Lutheran calendars.

churches.note: Not in the Anglican or Lutheran calendars

paras: Jewish tradition honours her more. The Talmud counts her among the seven prophetesses of Israel, with Sarah, Miriam, Deborah, Hannah, Huldah and Esther.

kin.name: Hannah
kin.text: In the same book, she too called herself a servant and asked to be remembered: “remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant.”

kin.name: Esther
kin.text: She too went before a man with power over life and death, to plead for lives: “And if I perish, I perish!”

kin.name: Rahab
kin.text: She too acted on her own to save a household, and asked the spies to “spare the lives of my father and mother.”
